keith: FYI - after the 03:12 deploy the serving runtime shows a perf regression for a subset of requests. tokens/sec dropped on some routes when the kernel selector chose flash-v3 over fused for short prefixes. sample: 2400 -> 1800 tok/s on g4dn (seq 256 workloads).

jun: Oof. Any KV-cache changes in this deploy?

keith: No direct KV changes. Early signal is kernel swap + batching heuristics interacting with eviction. KV hit-rate for the failing traffic dropped from ~72% to ~49% around the same time. That increases tokens/req and triggers different kernel paths.

maria: Can you paste profiler output and the selector decision log?

keith: Pasting the profiler snippet and kernel decision tail:

```
PROFILE SUMMARY (canary-node-7):
- route: /chat/stream
- median_seq: 256
- batching: dynamic 64->128
- kernel chosen: flash-v3 (60% cases), fused-attn (40%)
- tokens/sec (flash-v3): 1.8k
- tokens/sec (fused-attn): 2.4k
- GPU util (flash-v3): 58%
- GPU util (fused): 73%
- KV cache hit rate (before): 72.1% \n- KV cache hit rate (after): 48.9%\n```

keith: Selector log tail: `kernel_selector: picked flash-v3 because estimated_memory < threshold && seq_est >= 200`

sara: So selector favored flash-v3 for seq >=200, but fused is faster on these inputs? Guess kernel perf model is off for this region.

jun: Also suspect batching heuristic: when KV hit drops, effective sequence length increases and batching grows which changes kernel perf envelope. We need to repro with: seq 128/256/512 with and without KV hits.

perfbot: perfbot: dashboard update -> https://perf.redwood.local/dash/attn-kernel/1913456789 (shows tokens/sec and $/M tokens spike at 03:12) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

keith: Cost impact: $/M tokens baseline ~$1.05 -> peaked ~$1.48 for the impacted route. That's a ~41% delta.

maria: Can we isolate: (1) force selector to prefer fused for seq<=512 and (2) run a KV-preserve canary?

keith: Quick local repro steps I used:
```
# run micro-bench
./tools/profile --kernel=flash-v3 --seq=256 --batch=64 --kv-hit=0.5
./tools/profile --kernel=fused-attn --seq=256 --batch=64 --kv-hit=0.5
```
Both runs on same instance (p4d-sim) show fused ~33% faster.

jun: Suggest adding a small guard in kernel selector: if fused_latency_est * 1.05 < flash_latency_est then pick fused. Also add logging for kv_hit_est in selection key.

maria: Agreed. Also we should not conflate flash-v3 freshness with correctness. Maybe the new kernels have different tiling thresholds that penalize low-util scenarios.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026 - attn-kernel routing regression. Assigned to @keith, @maria.

keith: I'm going to roll a targeted canary change to bias selector toward fused for route `/chat/stream` and seq <= 512. Rolling at 11:30 UTC. Will monitor tokens/sec and $/M tokens.

sara: Can you add a short-term mitigation to the autoscaler: cap batch growth when kv_hit drops below 60% to avoid pathological batching induced by longer effective seq?

keith: Good call. Adding that now.

jun: After canary, we should run a matrix to update kernel performance model: seq=[64,128,256,512,1024], kv_hit=[0.2,0.5,0.8], batch=[32,64,128]. Capture tokens/sec and gpu_util. I'll script it.

maria: Also update cost dashboard to show $/M tokens broken down by kernel variant so we can track decisions over time.

keith: Timeline: canary bias at 11:30, run perf matrix 12:00-13:30, update models and revert if no improvement.

perfbot: perfbot: canary metric snapshot posted to channel in 5m.

sara: Thanks. If noisy, we can temporarily pin the route to fused in Dedicated pools until kernel models are fixed. :thumbsup:

keith: TL;DR - kernel selector mis-estimated perf region for flash-v3 when KV hit dropped -> tokens/sec down -> $/M up. Canary to prefer fused on short-to-mid seq. Full profiling matrix to follow.

jun: I'll own the matrix + model update. Assigning PR for selector guard to me.

keith: Assigned. Keeping channel updated.

sara: Thanks team.
